What is the minimum PoE budget needed on a switch to support 6 (six) APs that can only be powered using IEEE 802.3at if no other details are provided?
Using the IEEE 802.3at maximum PSE allocation of 30 W per AP, six APs require 6 × 30 W = 180 W of switch PoE budget.
In high-density environments, such as stadiums and convention centers, what extra factor has to be taken into account that can attenuate Wi-Fi signals when these environments are having an event?
People absorb and scatter RF energy. A dense crowd can change propagation and reduce received signal levels compared with an empty venue.
What document is typically created to launch a project?
A project charter formally authorizes the work and records its objectives, scope, stakeholders, and high-level responsibilities.

Your new customer is concerned about maintaining privacy for their proprietary information when you conduct information gathering for their WLAN design. Which document can you use to directly address their concern?
A nondisclosure agreement establishes a confidentiality obligation and limits how the customer's proprietary information may be shared.

Your customer is using PSK as their only authentication. They have an industry requirement to move to a stronger solution. Your recommendation is to move to a certificate-based type of authentication where both the client and server require certificates. Which EAP type would be the best fit?
EAP-TLS uses mutual certificate authentication: both the authentication server and the client prove their identity with certificates.

A company wants to connect its headquarters to its remote office that is 13 kilometers away using a wireless bridge. What requirement must not be forgotten by their Wireless Engineer when considering the Fresnel Zone?
Earth curvature raises the terrain-equivalent path over long distances. The link design must include this Earth bulge when calculating antenna height and Fresnel-zone clearance.
You are conducting a physical site survey where heavy machinery is repaired. What is a common item required specifically for this type of survey?
Site-survey and installation work must follow the facility's access rules and use appropriate personal protective equipment for the hazards present.

A business traveler from North America is in Europe. The hotel only provides coverage in 2.4 GHz. The traveler connects to the hotel's SSID and notices an AP in the hotel room. However, the laptop reports a very low RSSI when connected. The traveler does not have the same problem when connecting in the lobby. What would be the most likely cause of the low RSSI in the hotel room?
The AP in the room is using ZigBee instead of Wi-Fi.
The AP in the room is transmitting on channel 13 and the traveler associated to a non-channel 13 AP located elsewhere.
The switchport that the AP is connected to is only capable of transmitting at 10 Mbps.
The AP in the room is using Bluetooth instead of Wi-Fi.
Channel 13 is permitted in many European regulatory domains but is not available to some North American client configurations. Region settings can therefore prevent discovery.
A museum wants to offer Wi-Fi to its visitors. One of their requirements is to have the APs blend into the design of the museum. What should you do to meet this requirement?
Lock the AP inside of a metal box
Place the APs in between walls and I-beams
Use an 802.11b AP, so it looks old enough to be in a museum
Use a plastic cover that could blend in with the environment
A purpose-designed nonmetallic cover can improve appearance while avoiding the severe RF attenuation caused by metal enclosures; manufacturer guidance and warranty terms still apply.

An engineering firm just upgraded their WLAN from nine 802.11n APS to nine 802.11ac APs. After this upgrade, they did not see any improvement in throughput. What is the most likely cause of this result?
APs are transmitting at a low transmit power
APs are mounted on the wall
The APs are still using the 5 GHz lower band
A faster AP cannot deliver the newer PHY's benefits to legacy clients that lack the corresponding radio capabilities.

You and 10 other people are connected to a public hot-spot. You issue a ping sweep on the network, but you can't find any devices on the same subnet as yours. What feature might be enabled on the WLAN infrastructure that is preventing you from communicating with other devices on that subnet?
Client isolation prevents wireless stations on the same WLAN from communicating directly with one another, even though they share the SSID or subnet.

During an RFP analysis, one of the vendors mentioned that you'll need to upgrade your Gigabit Ethernet switches to MultiGig switches to ensure support for 802.11ac and 802.11ax, which both offer data rates over 1Gbps. Why is this not sound advice?
Because neither of the technologies support data rates over 1Gbps
Management overhead that is normal in WLANs will reduce the throughput of the client devices
Because 802.11ac only supports one spatial stream

The answer key points to WLAN management overhead as a throughput consideration. Management frames consume airtime that is shared with client data, so usable throughput is lower than the raw PHY rate.

A customer is acquiring a new VoWLAN system to replace their existing wired phone system. When reading about his system's requirements, you learned that is requires 25 db of SNR to work as expected. After surveying the environment, you discovered that the noise floor is -88 dBm. What should be the minimum RSSI value to meet the system's requirements?
For a 25 dB SNR requirement with a measured noise floor of −88 dBm, the required signal is −63 dBm.
You're about to deploy an Enterprise-class VoWLAN infrastructure. You need to ensure that QoS is properly configured throughout the network. What Access Category (AC) should voice frames/packets use?
AC_VO is the WMM voice access category. It receives the most favorable contention parameters to reduce delay for latency-sensitive voice packets.
After importing a floor plan to a predictive design tool, what should be done prior to adding APs, antennas and attenuators (e.g., walls)?
Set the transmit power for all APs
Nothing; just begin by adding APs, antenna and attenuators
Calibrate the floor plan to increase accuracy
A predictive model needs a correctly scaled and calibrated floor plan so distances, wall locations, and attenuation are represented accurately.

Your customer's 802.11n laptops are not able to see the SSID in the 5 GHz band in the conference room. When doing a walkthrough using one of these laptops, you confirm that it is unable to see the SSID in the 5 GHz band in the conference room. When using your own 802.11 ac laptop, you're able to see the SSID. What is the most likely cause of this problem?
The AP is configured to use channel 36
The customer laptop does not support Transmit Beamforming
Some legacy 5 GHz client radios do not support channel 144. If the AP uses that channel, those clients may not discover the SSID.
When designing a static channel plan for an office using voice devices near an airport, which range of channels should be avoided to ensure optimal performance when implemented?
Channels 116–124 are DFS channels in the 5 GHz band. Radar detection can force channel changes, which may disrupt real-time voice clients.

What is the most suitable antenna option to be used when designing a WLAN infrastructure with APs mounted on a ceiling with a height of more than 20 feet and having all of the client stations used from the floor?
A ceiling-mounted patch antenna directs more energy toward the floor area than a broad omnidirectional pattern, making it useful for high-ceiling deployments where clients are below the AP.
When using a predictive design tool, you have selected APs with an antenna gain 3 dBi and set the transmit power of the predicted APs to 25 mW. What should be EIRP of the APs in the design?
25 mW is approximately 14 dBm; adding 3 dBi antenna gain yields 17 dBm EIRP when no cable loss is specified.

Switches and APs have already been chosen by your customer. All switches support 802.3bz MultiGig interfaces and APs are 4x4:4 802.11ac wave 2 capable of using dual-5GHz and have one MultiGig interface. Some cable drops for the APs will run for more than 180.5 feet (or 55 meters). To support MultiGig, what is the best choice of cabling?
The cabling choice must support the required Ethernet rate over the actual channel length. Use the cable category and distance limits specified for the target PHY.
